modelResponse.episodeSummary: Robert D. Hale, 68M, in Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) with pulseless, hemodynamically collapsed status.
keyECGEvidence: morphology: No organized QRS; coarse fibrillatory waves ~5 Hz
stDeviationMm: ST elevation 4 mm V2–V4 on rhythm strip 90 s pre-arrest
preEventNote: Runs of PVCs then R-on-T preceded onset; 12-lead 8 min prior showed anterior ST elevation
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) leading to lethal arrhythmia.
modelResponse.mechanism: Myocardial ischemia/infarction (evidenced by ST elevation and elevated troponin) triggered ventricular irritability (PVCs) and R-on-T phenomenon, culminating in VF.
contributingFactors: History of Coronary artery disease and prior anterior MI

rejectedAlternatives.why: ECG shows coarse fibrillatory waves (VF) rather than an organized but pulseless rhythm.

recommendedActions: Initiate immediate ACLS protocols (Defibrillation for VF)
Establish large-bore IV access and provide high-flow oxygen
Prepare for immediate reperfusion (PCI or fibrinolysis) following stabilization
uncertainty: Blood pressure and SpO2 are unavailable due to 'no pulse; arterial line flat' status.
